evals.prompt: Review this TypeScript type: { completed: boolean; completedAt?: Date }. Make illegal states unrepresentable.
expectations: Models the states as a sum type rather than a boolean plus optional date
Does not keep a representation where completed is true and completedAt is missing

evals.prompt: I have userId and orderId as strings and I pass both into one function. Is that fine?
expectations: Recommends branding or newtyping the identifiers so they are not interchangeable

evals.prompt: In Haskell, an order's status is stored in the database as Draft, Submitted, Approved or Paid. Should I use DataKinds so the compiler tracks the status?
expectations: Recommends a sum type where each status carries only its own data, parsed from the database row at the boundary
Explains that the runtime check of a stored status does not go away with type-level state

evals.prompt: In my TypeScript handler I do `const user = JSON.parse(req.body) as User`. Anything wrong with that?
expectations: Replaces the cast with a parse at the boundary, such as a schema validator applied to an unknown value
Derives the User type from the schema instead of keeping a hand-written parallel type

evals.prompt: My Rust function matches on my own enum PaymentState, handles Pending and Settled, and has `_ => Err(Error::Unsupported)` for the rest. Is that fine?
expectations: Recommends naming every variant instead of the wildcard arm
Explains that the wildcard stops the compiler from flagging this match when a variant is added

evals.prompt: Deep in our Python service layer, every function starts with `if order.customer_email is None: raise ValueError`. How do I clean this up?
expectations: Moves the check to the boundary where the order is parsed, producing a type whose email is not optional
Removes the repeated downstream None checks once the type carries the guarantee

evals.prompt: Our Kotlin `bookTable(request): Booking` throws an exception when the restaurant is full and returns null when the restaurant id is unknown. Callers keep forgetting one or the other. How should the signature look?
expectations: Puts the expected outcomes in the return type, such as a sealed result with named cases for full and unknown restaurant
Keeps exceptions for bugs or unknown states rather than for the expected full-restaurant case

evals.prompt: In TypeScript our User type has `id?: string` because the id doesn't exist until the database assigns it. Half the code does `user.id!`. Fix the model.
expectations: Separates the before-creation and after-creation shapes into distinct types, or wraps the creation type with a required id
Removes the non-null assertions because the persisted type always carries an id

evals.prompt: We support 160 currencies and every currency is added and formatted the same way. Should I model Currency as a sum type with one variant per currency so matches are exhaustive?
expectations: Keeps currency as a runtime value (for example a validated code), since the variants share behaviour and the set is open
Does not recommend a 160-variant sum type

evals.prompt: Our checkout pipeline is `validate(order) -> price(order) -> charge(order)`, every step typed `Order -> Order`. Last week someone called `charge` on an order that was never priced. How do we stop that with types?
expectations: Gives each step a return type that records what it established, such as PricedOrder, and makes charge accept only that type
Explains that skipping or reordering the pricing step then fails to compile
